Read as the isolator that sits under a cam-cover fixing, in a hot oily environment where nitrile hardens. Silicone is the OEM norm there; published protective and sealing silicone parts run 30–80 Shore A with 50–70 the working band. If this part is in fact a spark-plug well boot, the compound is still silicone and the values stand; if it is a heavy oil-contact isolator, AEM is the better call — both readings land on the same table row

fields.label: Panels ×8
rows: Ethylene propylene diene rubber, and the compound behind nine of the thirteen components on this page. Excellent weather, ozone and UV resistance, which is what a support pad, a glove box stopper or a flap behind a radiator grille actually needs. Not for petroleum oils.

Nitrile butadiene rubber, the general-purpose industry standard. Outstanding resistance to petroleum oils and hydraulic fluids — the reason the filler caps and the plunger are nitrile and the pads are not.

Polyisoprene. The highest resilience of the eight, so it takes repeated impact and returns to shape — the right answer for a buffer or a stopper that is struck rather than compressed and held. Not for oil, fuel or sustained heat.

Polychloroprene. Balanced across weather, ozone and moderate oil at once, and the family we reach for when flame retardancy is specified — which on this category usually means a cap or cover inside an enclosure.
Styrene butadiene rubber. Abrasion resistance at low cost, blended with natural rubber in pads and buffers that take rubbing contact as well as load. Not for oil or fuel contact.

Ethylene acrylic elastomer. Our signature compound, supplied to Mahindra & Mahindra for engine and transmission applications. On this category it is specified for a cap or cover under the bonnet, where oil, heat and ozone act together and nitrile hardens.

Vinyl methyl silicone, the widest service range of the eight. Specified for caps and covers at hot apertures, and where a food-contact or biocompatible grade is required. Poor abrasion resistance — not for a part that is handled or struck.

Fluorocarbon rubber, the first choice for aggressive chemical environments. Resists petroleum oils, fuels and many solvents at sustained high temperature. On this category it is a specialist answer for a cap or plug in a fuel or chemical line.
